ownEvidence.title: The Fraunhofer contract-research model
ownEvidence.claim: Germany funds the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft's institutes in proportion to what they earn from industry, and in 2025 the society performed 3.2 billion euros of contract research, 966 million euros of it paid by industry.

ownEvidence.title: Kurzarbeit in the 2008-2009 crisis
ownEvidence.claim: Germany answered the 2008-2009 collapse in manufacturing orders by paying firms to cut hours instead of jobs, and short-time work covered 1.44 million workers at the May 2009 peak, about 5 percent of insured employment, while unemployment barely rose.

ownEvidence.title: THW, volunteer civil protection as a federal institution
ownEvidence.claim: Germany's federal civil-protection agency trains and equips a volunteer force that reached about 88,000 people across 669 local units in May 2025, supported by about 2,200 paid staff.

ownEvidence.title: Federal siren warning network, and its dismantling
ownEvidence.claim: West Germany built a federal warning service after 1955; after the Cold War the federally owned service was dissolved, its ten warning offices were abandoned and the nationwide siren alarm network was dismantled or transferred to municipalities, ending a system that had relied on about 1,700 volunteer helpers.
